take_homes: What I tell the model up front steers every answer after it. A file it reads each session saves me retyping my background.
The model flatters its own work, so its self-review is a hypothesis. My own knowledge of the subject is the check.
Specific gripes (my hate list) pull output away from the generic version much better than abstract descriptions.

monday.move: Probably nothing. Maybe paste my own hate list and one real document into a chat to see if the output differs.
monday.when: Some quiet half hour, not Monday morning
monday.stop_condition: If the result reads like the generic version, I drop it
monday.blocker: Calendar full of steering groups; a website about myself is not a work problem.

misconception.why: The module said openly what does not work (self-review is flattering) and let me test it. The tool is still a tool, and I'm not sure it changes my job, but 'it will blow over' feels less safe.

one_line: Less slide-ware than I feared; the bit where it admits the model flatters itself was honest, but I haven't yet seen anything that touches my actual work.
